name: ELSA Speak
tagline: Record pronunciation practice and provide limited acoustic feedback without diagnostic claims

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 30 practice lessons/exercises on official comparison pages; limited AI role-play, coaching, and feedback
tiers.notes: ELSA's main page labels several free features only as limited; 30 is the clearest numeric cap published on its own comparison pages.

tiers.name: ELSA Pro
tiers.limits: 9,000+ lessons on the current shop comparison; personalized learning path; pronunciation feedback; 25,000+ exercises across 220+ topics on the product page
tiers.notes: Standard one-year web price is $89.99; official pages conflict on the exact lesson count (5,000+, 8,000+, or 9,000+), so the current shop headline is used.

tiers.name: ELSA Premium
tiers.limits: 10,000+ targeted lessons and 25,000+ exercises on the current shop; unlimited AI role-play; Speech Analyzer; certificate courses
tiers.notes: Standard one-year web price is $99.99; other official campaign pages show lower or region-specific first-term offers.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 30 practice lessons/exercises; AI role-play, coaching, and feedback are limited
pricing.billingTerms: Annual web subscriptions shown at standard rates; mobile and campaign pages also sell monthly/multi-month terms; 7-day trial; auto-renewal varies by storefront
pricing.hiddenCosts: ELSA runs many first-cycle, affiliate, regional, and app-store promotions with materially different prices; promotional rates may renew at a higher standard rate and lesson-count claims conflict across its own live pages.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For ELSA Speak, record pronunciation practice and provide limited acoustic feedback without diagnostic claims. The hard boundary is proprietary speech models, curriculum, scoring data, mobile polish, and coaching, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Record pronunciation practice from user-supplied material, provide limited acoustic feedback, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without diagnostic claims or claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: proprietary speech models, curriculum, scoring data, mobile polish, and coaching
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for ELSA Speak because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Moodle
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source learning platform with courses, assessments, and progress tracking.

alternatives.name: Speechling
alternatives.desc: Native-audio imitation, side-by-side recordings and a small monthly ration of human pronunciation coaching.

facts.engines: Human pronunciation coaches plus proprietary speech processing; no acoustic model or backend is named publicly
facts.dataFormat: Recordings, practice history and coach feedback in the user's Speechling cloud account/audio journal; the underlying storage format is not published
facts.gapVsPaid: Speechling's strongest feedback is human and therefore delayed and rationed on the free service, not instant phoneme-level AI scoring after every attempt.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.desc: Records your voice beside reference audio for honest comparison, but does not invent a dubious pronunciation diagnosis.

facts.install: Use the Windows installer, macOS DMG or official Linux launcher
facts.dataFormat: Local profile files including collection.anki2, collection.media and backups; exports use .apkg/.colpkg, with optional AnkiWeb sync
facts.gapVsPaid: Anki can record and compare speech but provides no automatic phoneme-level diagnosis, personalized scoring or corrective coaching.

alternatives.name: AnkiDroid
alternatives.desc: Mobile listen-and-record practice using your own cards; feedback comes from your ears rather than an AI score.

facts.install: Install from Google Play or F-Droid, or sideload the official APK
facts.dataFormat: An Anki collection and media on the Android device, with .apkg import/export and optional AnkiWeb sync
facts.gapVsPaid: AnkiDroid records and replays speech but supplies no automatic phoneme diagnosis, score or corrective coaching.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for ELSA Speak in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: record pronunciation practice from user-supplied material, provide limited acoustic feedback, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without diagnostic claims or claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
